## Verdict

Inkwell costs least for a team of 22, at $242 per month. Its 20-seat minimum sits below the team size, so all 22 seats bill at the list rate of $11. Dorado is $528 and Borealis is $600, the latter forcing payment for 18 seats the team will not use.

## Vendor pricing

| Vendor | Price per seat | Minimum seats |
|---|---|---|
| Dorado | $24 | 5 |
| Inkwell | $11 | 20 |
| Borealis | $15 | 40 |

## Cost at this size

Seats paid for is the team size (22) or the vendor minimum, whichever is larger.

- **Dorado:** minimum 5 is below 22, so 22 seats paid. 22 × $24 = **$528 per month**.
- **Inkwell:** minimum 20 is below 22, so 22 seats paid. 22 × $11 = **$242 per month**.
- **Borealis:** minimum 40 exceeds 22, so 40 seats paid. 40 × $15 = **$600 per month**. Effective rate $27.27 per person ($600 ÷ 22).

Inkwell is $286 per month cheaper than Dorado and $358 cheaper than Borealis — $3,432 and $4,296 over twelve months.

## Risks

Borealis is penalised here by a minimum, not by its rate. At 40 people it bills $600 against Inkwell's $440 and Dorado's $960, so it never overtakes Inkwell on list price, but the gap narrows sharply with growth. Dorado's $24 seat is the dearest on the list at every size above 5 seats.

The team sits just two people above Inkwell's 20-seat floor. Any shrinkage below 20 means paying for unused seats, and at 18 people or fewer Dorado's 5-seat minimum would make it the more flexible option on headcount, though still more expensive at this range.

This compares price only. The price list carries nothing on features, support, limits or contract terms, so a cheaper seat may buy less. Figures assume monthly billing as stated; annual commitments or discounts are not covered and could reorder the ranking.
